clues: A protected tropical landscape combines an exceptional variety of palms with vast spaces beneath the ground.
Its explored caves shelter large populations of bats and cave swiftlets.
Karst landforms and numerous vegetation zones make it valuable to both geologists and biologists.
The park lies in Sarawak on Borneo and includes an exceptionally large chamber known as Sarawak Chamber.
Find the Malaysian national park named for a 2,377-metre sandstone mountain and celebrated for its immense caves.
targetLabel: Gunung Mulu National Park — designated property reference point
modernContext: UNESCO’s published representative point for the designated property, not its uniquely correct centre.
explanation: The park combines tropical biodiversity with a major karst and cave landscape. Its named summit is sandstone, so the clues do not imply that every rock within the park is limestone. The published park reference point is the target, rather than an inaccessible underground chamber.
dateLabel: First UNESCO World Heritage inscription year, not the age of the natural feature
cultures: Physical geography, conservation and scientific study
uncertainty: Source-checked authoring only; independent factual, English and clue-order review is pending. The point represents the designated property, not every part of a large natural feature. Source descriptions and dynamic environmental conditions may differ in date or extent; precise current measurements are not implied.
